**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 17, 2026**
**Member:** Reese Carter
**Member ID:** W769161738
**Reference number:** POC-9992A0803A-86478
**Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin

---

To the Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Molina Healthcare's denial of the prior authorization request my surgeon submitted for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030). I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve this surgery.

**A note on the policy and criteria.** The denial notice states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not name that policy or tell me what the criteria actually require. Because the specific criteria applied to my case have not been given to me, I am not able to quote the plan's own language back to it in this letter, and I have not tried to guess at it. Nothing in this letter should be read as a quotation from any Molina policy. What I can do is set out, in plain terms, what is in my medical record — and ask the plan to identify the standard it says that record failed to meet.

**Request for the criteria used, in writing.** Molina's utilization management information states that its review criteria are MCG criteria available through the secure provider portal, and that a person may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the MCG guideline title and the criteria applied to my determination**, along with the specific items of documentation the reviewer found to be missing. The plan holds those criteria; I do not. If my request was denied because something was absent from the file, I am asking Molina to say what that something is, so that it can be supplied.

**The denial reason given was incomplete documentation. Here is what the record contains.**

The notice does not say that my condition fails a clinical standard — it says the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I would ask the reviewer to look again at the prior authorization packet, which documents the following:

- **Duration and course of symptoms.** 18 months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised conservative care.** Supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 10 weeks, from April 24, 2026 to July 3, 2026, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication and injection trials.** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on May 7, 2026, which gave 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging.** MRI of the lumbar spine on June 23, 2026 showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Physical examination.** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.
- **Functional impact.** I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain into my right calf.
- **Surgical risk factors.** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Taken together, the record shows a symptomatic problem of long duration, a documented course of non-surgical treatment that was tried and did not give lasting relief, imaging that identifies a specific structural cause, and an examination finding that corresponds to the level seen on that imaging. These are the elements that a medical necessity review for a decompression would ordinarily look for. If the plan's criteria set a particular threshold — a required number of weeks, visits, or treatment types — that threshold has not been stated to me, and I cannot address a number I have not been shown. I am asking the plan either to identify it or to review the record as it stands.

**If documentation is genuinely missing, I am asking for the chance to supply it.** Neither I nor my surgeon was told which document the reviewer could not locate. If a chart note, a therapy record, the MRI report, or an operative plan did not reach the reviewer's file, please tell me which one, and I will ask Dr. Reyes's office to send it directly. A denial based on an incomplete file can be resolved by completing the file, and I would like the opportunity to do that.

**What I am asking for.** I request that Molina Healthcare overturn the denial of August 17, 2026 (reference number POC-9992A0803A-86478) and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes. In the alternative, I request that the plan provide me in writing with the MCG guideline title and criteria applied, the credentials of the reviewer who made this determination, and an itemized list of the documentation said to be missing, and that my appeal be held open so that any such documentation can be submitted.

I understand this appeal must be received by **February 13, 2027**, as stated in the denial notice. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on that notice, which I understand to be the authoritative address; I can also submit or follow up through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com or by calling the Member Services number on my ID card.

Please send your written determination to me at the address above. I am happy to provide any authorization needed for Dr. Reyes's office to speak with the plan directly about the clinical record.

Thank you for taking a second look at this.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
Reese Carter
Member ID: W769161738
Date of birth: [my date of birth]
Phone: [my phone number]
Date: [date signed]

**Enclosures:** [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-17] · [MRI lumbar spine report, 2026-06-23] · [physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03] · [office notes from Dr. Reyes] · [injection record, 2026-05-07] · [any other records I am including]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
